To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TCR triggering in T lymphocyte results in caspase activation, even in the absence of cell death.

caspase activation and proteolysis of caspase substrates occur during T cell stimulation, in the absence of DNA fragmentation and cell death, suggesting a role for caspases in lymphocyte proliferation and differentiation.

the caspases, a family of cysteine proteinases, are activated in lymphocytes after T cell receptor (or B cell receptor) triggering, and that this activation is an essential step in lymphocyte proliferation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the cysteine protease family of caspases in the regulation of cell death.
the activation of the cysteine protease caspase-3 during T cell activation.
the role of caspase activity in lymphocyte stimulation and proliferation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the activation of caspase-3, and to a lesser extent of caspase 6 and 7, is a common feature of T cell activation.
caspase activation occurs in nonapoptotis cells and is not restricted to apoptotic cells, and is not a marker of apoptosis.
caspase activation occurs in viable, stimulated T lymphocytes and is associated with a physiological response that does not necessarily lead to apoptosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
caspase activation in nonapoptosis is an early response to T cell activation.
caspase processing is an early event during TCR triggering, which occurs in nonapoptosis T cells.
TCR triggering activates a caspase pathway that is distinct from apoptosis, and is involved in the control of cell cycle progression and lymphocyte activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
caspase activation occurs during T cell activation, and this activation is required for normal T cell function.
caspases are activated early during T cell stimulation, in the absence of cell death, as demonstrated by their proteolytic activation in the presence of the broad caspase inhibitor zVAD.
caspase activation occurs in viable lymphocytes during stimulation, and is involved in the regulation of early steps of the T cell activation program.
